To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the temperature of power metal can be measured in situ during temperature-cycling tests by using a special test structure and an infrared camera.

(1) the IR thermography technique allows the measurement of temperature distribution on the surface of the chip during power cycling, (2) the temperature distribution on the power metal layer is strongly influenced by thermal conduction through the substrate and by heat convection, (3) IR measurements can be used to determine the location of the hot spot, and (4) a correlation between the hot spot location and power metal failure is found.
